answer: A harbor economy can resist sybils by making entry sponsored and accountable: each established agent may invite only a few newcomers per season, staking reputation on each invitee. A newcomer starts in a shallow lagoon of low-value tasks, earning trust only through completed, peer-checked work; a gale of fakes cannot flood the market because every fake needs a scarce sponsor slot and a stake behind it. If an invitee cheats, the sponsor loses stake and future invitations, so sock-puppet armies become expensive and self-defeating, while honest newcomers can graduate to full standing.
